articles.title: The walkable city: Discovering Beijing at street level
articles.titleCn: 步行城市：在街头发现北京
articles.summary: The walkable city: Discovering Beijing at street level
articles.summaryCn: 本文探讨了北京步行友好性的重要性，强调城市设计、绿化和社区规划如何影响人们选择步行作为日常生活的一部分。

Walk a few blocks in Beijing and the city begins to {{0}} itself differently. Buildings that seem distant from a car become part of the {{1}}. Parks become shortcuts.

paragraphs.en: A neighborhood that might look like a collection of apartment blocks becomes a network of restaurants, small shops, public spaces and everyday {{2}}. Walking slows the city down enough to notice it. And increasingly, cities around the world are paying attention to what happens when people are encouraged to move this way. For Beijing, the question is not simply whether people can walk from one place to another. It is whether the city can make walking convenient, comfortable and {{3}} enough that people choose it as part of everyday life.

paragraphs.cn: 这种区别很重要。仅有人行道并不能使城市适合步行。北京的海淀公园汇集了跑步者、家庭和各年龄段的步行者，展示了城市绿色空间如何将日常出行变成城市生活中诱人的一部分。步行友好性常常被简化为距离：一个人在一定时间内可以步行多远。但城市研究者关注更广泛的因素，包括连通性、公共交通可达性、土地利用多样性、街道设计、安全性、绿化和日常服务的邻近性。

paragraphs.en: One increasingly {{8}} concept is the 15-minute neighborhood, where residents can reach basic services and {{9}} within roughly 15 minutes on foot. Research examining Chinese cities has found that the idea has increasingly become part of discussions about healthy community planning. A 2019 study published in the Journal of Transport & Health examined 15-minute walkable neighborhoods in urban China and linked the concept to efforts to encourage walking and improve public health. The idea is simple: if a person can reach a supermarket, school, park, restaurant, health service or public transport within a reasonable walk, walking becomes less of an exercise activity and more of a normal part of daily life. That is perhaps the most important distinction.
paragraphs.cn: 一个越来越有影响力的概念是“15分钟生活圈”，即居民可以在大约15分钟步行范围内到达基本服务和设施。研究中国城市的研究发现，这一概念已越来越多地成为健康社区规划讨论的一部分。2019年发表在《交通与健康杂志》上的一项研究考察了中国城市的15分钟步行社区，并将这一概念与鼓励步行和改善公共健康的努力联系起来。这个想法很简单：如果一个人可以在合理的步行范围内到达超市、学校、公园、餐馆、医疗服务或公共交通，那么步行就不再是一种锻炼活动，而是日常生活的一部分。这也许是最重要的区别。

paragraphs.en:
You don't necessarily have to decide to "go for a walk." You simply walk because that's how you get somewhere. Visitors stroll along a shaded lakeside path at Beihai Park in Beijing, where dense tree canopies and waterfront paths offer a cool, inviting space for everyday walks and leisure. Beijing at walking speed
This is something I have noticed while exploring Beijing on foot. The city can feel enormous when viewed from a subway map. But walking breaks that scale into smaller pieces.
paragraphs.cn: 你不一定非要决定“去散步”。你只是走路，因为那是你到达某处的方式。游客在北京北海公园一条绿树成荫的湖边小径上漫步，茂密的树冠和滨水步道为日常散步和休闲提供了凉爽宜人的空间。这是我在北京步行探索时注意到的事情。从地铁图上看，这座城市可能显得巨大。但步行将这种规模分解成更小的部分。

paragraphs.en: A subway station exit leads to a residential street. A busy intersection gives way to a tree-lined road. A park becomes a shortcut between two neighborhoods. A river creates a natural corridor through the city. The experience is different from running, too.
paragraphs.cn: 一个地铁站出口通向一条住宅街道。一个繁忙的十字路口让位于一条绿树成荫的道路。一个公园成为两个街区之间的捷径。一条河流在城市中形成一条自然走廊。这种体验也与跑步不同。

paragraphs.en: Running gives you {{10}}. Walking gives you time. You notice elderly residents gathering beneath trees, people stopping for breakfast, delivery riders making their rounds and children playing in neighborhood parks. You hear conversations that would disappear into the background at a faster pace.You notice the small businesses that serve a neighborhood rather than a tourist. None of these things necessarily make headlines.
paragraphs.cn: 跑步给你动力。步行给你时间。你会注意到老人在树下聚集，人们停下来吃早餐，外卖骑手在送餐，孩子们在社区公园玩耍。你会听到那些在更快速度下会消失在背景中的对话。你会注意到那些服务于社区而非游客的小生意。这些事情本身不一定能成为头条新闻。

paragraphs.en:
But together, they make up the city. And that is where walkability becomes more than an urban-planning concept. It becomes a question about how people experience their surroundings. There is also a strong public-health argument.
paragraphs.cn: 但合在一起，它们构成了这座城市。这就是步行友好性超越城市规划概念的地方。它变成了一个关于人们如何体验周围环境的问题。在北京历史悠久的五道营胡同里晨间漫步，行人友好的街道将居民和游客与几步之内的当地餐馆、早餐店和社区商业连接起来。步行对健康也有强有力的公共健康论据。

paragraphs.en: Walking is one of the simplest forms of physical activity because it does not necessarily require a gym, special equipment or a training plan. The World Health Organization (WHO) identifies walking and cycling as forms of active mobility that can improve physical and mental wellbeing while reducing the risk of several {{12}} diseases. It also points to wider environmental benefits, including lower traffic congestion, improved air quality and reduced emissions. Green space can make that experience even more valuable. A WHO review says urban parks and other green spaces can support physical activity, psychological relaxation and social interaction while helping reduce {{15}} to heat, noise and air pollution.
paragraphs.cn: 步行是最简单的体育活动形式之一，因为它不一定需要健身房、特殊设备或训练计划。世界卫生组织（WHO）将步行和骑行视为积极出行形式，可以改善身心健康，同时降低多种非传染性疾病的风险。它还指出了更广泛的环境效益，包括减少交通拥堵、改善空气质量和减少排放。绿色空间可以使这种体验更有价值。WHO的一份综述指出，城市公园和其他绿色空间可以支持体育活动、心理放松和社交互动，同时有助于减少暴露于高温、噪音和空气污染。

paragraphs.en: Research conducted specifically in Beijing {{13}} that connection. A 2017 study examining urban parks in Beijing found that park users were more physically active than non-users in almost every form of physical activity measured, while having a park within 500 meters of home was significantly associated with physical activity. The researchers also found that physical activity and interaction with nature in parks were associated with mental-health benefits such as relaxation and improved self-perceived confidence. Another study, published in Frontiers in Public Health, examined data from Beijing residents and found that both perceived quality and {{14}} of urban green space were positively associated with self-rated health. Social interaction and perceptions of air quality were among the factors helping to explain that relationship.

Walk a few blocks in Beijing and the city begins to reveal itself differently. Buildings that seem distant from a car become part of the streetscape. Parks become shortcuts. A neighborhood that might look like a collection of apartment blocks becomes a network of restaurants, small shops, public spaces and everyday encounters.
Walking slows the city down enough to notice it.
And increasingly, cities around the world are paying attention to what happens when people are encouraged to move this way.
For Beijing, the question is not simply whether people can walk from one place to another. It is whether the city can make walking convenient, comfortable and appealing enough that people choose it as part of everyday life.
That distinction matters. A sidewalk alone does not make a city walkable.
Haidian Park in Beijing, brings together runners, families and walkers of all generations, showing how urban green spaces turn everyday movement into an inviting part of city life. 
More than getting from A to B
Walkability is often reduced to distance: how far someone can travel on foot within a certain amount of time.
But urban researchers look at a much wider range of factors, including connectivity, access to public transport, land-use diversity, street design, safety, greenery and proximity to everyday services.
One increasingly influential concept is the 15-minute neighborhood, where residents can reach basic services and amenities within roughly 15 minutes on foot.
Research examining Chinese cities has found that the idea has increasingly become part of discussions about healthy community planning. A 2019 study published in the Journal of Transport & Health examined 15-minute walkable neighborhoods in urban China and linked the concept to efforts to encourage walking and improve public health.
The idea is simple: if a person can reach a supermarket, school, park, restaurant, health service or public transport within a reasonable walk, walking becomes less of an exercise activity and more of a normal part of daily life.
That is perhaps the most important distinction. You don't necessarily have to decide to "go for a walk." You simply walk because that's how you get somewhere.
Visitors stroll along a shaded lakeside path at Beihai Park in Beijing, where dense tree canopies and waterfront paths offer a cool, inviting space for everyday walks and leisure. 
Beijing at walking speed
This is something I have noticed while exploring Beijing on foot.
The city can feel enormous when viewed from a subway map. But walking breaks that scale into smaller pieces.
A subway station exit leads to a residential street. A busy intersection gives way to a tree-lined road. A park becomes a shortcut between two neighborhoods. A river creates a natural corridor through the city.
The experience is different from running, too. Running gives you momentum. Walking gives you time.
You notice elderly residents gathering beneath trees, people stopping for breakfast, delivery riders making their rounds and children playing in neighborhood parks.
You hear conversations that would disappear into the background at a faster pace.You notice the small businesses that serve a neighborhood rather than a tourist.
None of these things necessarily make headlines. But together, they make up the city.
And that is where walkability becomes more than an urban-planning concept. It becomes a question about how people experience their surroundings.

The health case for walking
There is also a strong public-health argument.
Walking is one of the simplest forms of physical activity because it does not necessarily require a gym, special equipment or a training plan.
The World Health Organization (WHO) identifies walking and cycling as forms of active mobility that can improve physical and mental wellbeing while reducing the risk of several noncommunicable diseases. It also points to wider environmental benefits, including lower traffic congestion, improved air quality and reduced emissions.
Green space can make that experience even more valuable.
A WHO review says urban parks and other green spaces can support physical activity, psychological relaxation and social interaction while helping reduce exposure to heat, noise and air pollution.
Research conducted specifically in Beijing reinforces that connection.
A 2017 study examining urban parks in Beijing found that park users were more physically active than non-users in almost every form of physical activity measured, while having a park within 500 meters of home was significantly associated with physical activity. The researchers also found that physical activity and interaction with nature in parks were associated with mental-health benefits such as relaxation and improved self-perceived confidence.
Another study, published in Frontiers in Public Health, examined data from Beijing residents and found that both perceived quality and accessibility of urban green space were positively associated with self-rated health. Social interaction and perceptions of air quality were among the factors helping to explain that relationship.
The findings don't mean that simply living near a park automatically makes someone healthier. But they do point to an important relationship between access to green space, how people use it and how they feel afterward.
That matters in a city as large as Beijing.
A cyclist rides beneath a dense tree canopy along a Beijing street, where natural shade transforms ordinary roads into cool, inviting corridors for walking and cycling. 
Greenery matters more than we might think
There is an interesting detail in Beijing's walking environment that is easy to overlook: trees.
A shaded street can feel completely different from a wide, exposed road on a hot summer afternoon.
A small pocket of greenery can turn a route from somewhere you simply pass through into somewhere you want to linger. Research supports that observation.
A 2020 study of Beijing examined how street greenery affects active travel and found that greater greenery was associated with a higher probability of walking and cycling. The relationship was particularly relevant on lower-class roads, where traffic tends to be lighter and accessibility higher.
More recently, research published in Scientific Reports in 2025 examined street greenery and physical activity among older adults in Beijing, using street-view imagery and other data to investigate how exposure to greenery at street level relates to physical activity.
That suggests greenery does more than make a street look attractive. It can influence whether people choose to walk and how they experience the journey when they do.
This is one reason Beijing's expanding network of parks, greenways and riverside paths matters to the wider question of walkability.
But green infrastructure isn't automatically successful simply because it exists. People need to be able to reach it.
A park play area offers outdoor recreation just steps from residential communities, demonstrating how access to nearby green space supports physical activity and family wellbeing within a short walk from home. 
What I noticed by slowing down
That is perhaps what has surprised me most as my own journey has moved from running to walking. When I run through a city, I tend to think about distance. When I walk, I think about place.
I notice where people stop. I notice which streets feel inviting and which ones feel like somewhere you simply want to cross. I notice how quickly a dense urban environment can turn into a pocket of greenery.
And I notice how many different generations can occupy the same public space at the same time. That may be one of the most valuable things about walking.
It puts you at the same speed as the city around you.
The measure of a walkable city
Perhaps a walkable city isn't one where everyone walks everywhere. It is one where people have the choice.
Where an older person can comfortably reach a park. Where a child can move safely through their neighborhood. Where a commuter can combine the subway with a short walk. Where a resident can reach a shop without crossing a major road. Where greenery provides shade along the journey.
And where walking isn't treated solely as exercise.
It is simply part of living.
Beijing is still a vast, complex and rapidly changing city. Its roads are busy, its distances can be enormous and its neighborhoods vary considerably.
But at street level, another city exists.
It is quieter.
Slower.
And much more human.

这种区别很重要。仅有人行道并不能使城市适合步行。北京的海淀公园汇集了跑步者、家庭和各年龄段的步行者，展示了城市绿色空间如何将日常出行变成城市生活中诱人的一部分。步行友好性常常被简化为距离：一个人在一定时间内可以步行多远。但城市研究者关注更广泛的因素，包括连通性、公共交通可达性、土地利用多样性、街道设计、安全性、绿化和日常服务的邻近性。

一个越来越有影响力的概念是“15分钟生活圈”，即居民可以在大约15分钟步行范围内到达基本服务和设施。研究中国城市的研究发现，这一概念已越来越多地成为健康社区规划讨论的一部分。2019年发表在《交通与健康杂志》上的一项研究考察了中国城市的15分钟步行社区，并将这一概念与鼓励步行和改善公共健康的努力联系起来。这个想法很简单：如果一个人可以在合理的步行范围内到达超市、学校、公园、餐馆、医疗服务或公共交通，那么步行就不再是一种锻炼活动，而是日常生活的一部分。这也许是最重要的区别。

你不一定非要决定“去散步”。你只是走路，因为那是你到达某处的方式。游客在北京北海公园一条绿树成荫的湖边小径上漫步，茂密的树冠和滨水步道为日常散步和休闲提供了凉爽宜人的空间。这是我在北京步行探索时注意到的事情。从地铁图上看，这座城市可能显得巨大。但步行将这种规模分解成更小的部分。

一个地铁站出口通向一条住宅街道。一个繁忙的十字路口让位于一条绿树成荫的道路。一个公园成为两个街区之间的捷径。一条河流在城市中形成一条自然走廊。这种体验也与跑步不同。

跑步给你动力。步行给你时间。你会注意到老人在树下聚集，人们停下来吃早餐，外卖骑手在送餐，孩子们在社区公园玩耍。你会听到那些在更快速度下会消失在背景中的对话。你会注意到那些服务于社区而非游客的小生意。这些事情本身不一定能成为头条新闻。

但合在一起，它们构成了这座城市。这就是步行友好性超越城市规划概念的地方。它变成了一个关于人们如何体验周围环境的问题。在北京历史悠久的五道营胡同里晨间漫步，行人友好的街道将居民和游客与几步之内的当地餐馆、早餐店和社区商业连接起来。步行对健康也有强有力的公共健康论据。

步行是最简单的体育活动形式之一，因为它不一定需要健身房、特殊设备或训练计划。世界卫生组织（WHO）将步行和骑行视为积极出行形式，可以改善身心健康，同时降低多种非传染性疾病的风险。它还指出了更广泛的环境效益，包括减少交通拥堵、改善空气质量和减少排放。绿色空间可以使这种体验更有价值。WHO的一份综述指出，城市公园和其他绿色空间可以支持体育活动、心理放松和社交互动，同时有助于减少暴露于高温、噪音和空气污染。

专门在北京进行的研究强化了这一联系。2017年一项考察北京城市公园的研究发现，在几乎所有测量的体育活动形式中，公园使用者比非使用者更活跃，而家附近500米内有公园与体育活动显著相关。研究人员还发现，公园中的体育活动和与自然的互动与放松和改善自我感知信心等心理健康益处相关。另一项发表在《公共卫生前沿》上的研究考察了北京居民的数据，发现城市绿色空间的感知质量和可达性都与自评健康正相关。社交互动和对空气质量的感知是解释这种关系的因素之一。

这些发现并不意味着仅仅住在公园附近就能自动让人更健康。但它们确实指出了绿色空间的可达性、人们如何使用它以及事后感受之间的重要关系。这在像北京这样的大城市很重要。一名骑行者在北京一条街道上茂密的树冠下骑行，自然树荫将普通道路变成了适合步行和骑行的凉爽宜人的走廊。绿色植物的重要性可能超乎我们的想象。北京步行环境中有一个容易被忽视的有趣细节：树木。

在炎热的夏日午后，一条有树荫的街道与一条宽阔暴露的道路感觉完全不同。一小片绿色可以将一条路线从你只是经过的地方变成你想逗留的地方。研究支持这一观察。2020年一项关于北京的研究考察了街道绿化如何影响主动出行，发现更大的绿化与更高的步行和骑行概率相关。这种关系在交通较轻、可达性较高的低等级道路上尤其明显。

最近，2025年发表在《科学报告》上的研究考察了北京老年人的街道绿化和体育活动，使用街景图像和其他数据来调查街道层面的绿化暴露与体育活动的关系。这表明绿化不仅仅让街道看起来有吸引力。它可以影响人们是否选择步行以及他们步行时的体验。这是北京不断扩展的公园、绿道和滨河步道网络对更广泛的步行友好性问题重要的原因之一。但绿色基础设施并不会仅仅因为存在就自动成功。

人们需要能够到达它。一个公园游乐区提供距离住宅社区仅几步之遥的户外娱乐，展示了附近绿色空间的可达性如何在短距离步行内支持体育活动和家庭福祉。当我自己的旅程从跑步转向步行时，这也许是最让我惊讶的。当我跑步穿过城市时，我倾向于思考距离。当我走路时，我思考地点。

我注意到人们在哪里停下来。我注意到哪些街道让人感到舒适，哪些街道让人觉得你只想穿过。我注意到密集的城市环境如何迅速变成一片绿色。我注意到多少代人能同时占据同一个公共空间。这也许是步行最有价值的事情之一。

它让你与周围的城市处于同一速度。也许一个适合步行的城市不是每个人都步行去任何地方。它是一个人们有选择权的城市。一个老人可以舒适地到达公园。一个孩子可以安全地在社区里移动。

一个通勤者可以将地铁与短途步行结合起来。一个居民可以在不穿过主要道路的情况下到达商店。绿色植物在旅途中提供树荫。步行不仅仅被视为锻炼。它只是生活的一部分。

北京仍然是一个广阔、复杂且快速变化的城市。它的道路繁忙，距离可能巨大，社区差异很大。但在街头层面，存在另一座城市。它更安静。更慢。

而且更有人情味。编者按：Denique Daniëls是CGTN数字频道的多媒体编辑。本文是“中国进行时”专栏的一部分，该专栏通过运动——从跑步和步行到公共空间设计、健康文化和社区——探索当代中国生活。通过以人的节奏观察城市，该系列捕捉了日常习惯如何塑造在中国的体验。

articles.title: Why Chinese families are turning robot games into career days
articles.titleCn: 为什么中国家庭把机器人比赛变成职业日
articles.summary: Why Chinese families are turning robot games into career days
articles.summaryCn: 中国家庭带孩子观看世界人形机器人比赛，既是为了激发兴趣，也是为未来职业发展铺路。

paragraphs.en: At the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, the robots were supposed to be the stars, {{0}} down tracks and breaking records, {{1}} through obstacle courses, scoring goals, breaking into cheerleading dances and occasionally {{2}} their way through the competition. But amid the packed stands and nonstop demonstrations, another {{3}} kept catching my eye – the sheer number of children in the audience excitedly crowding the barriers, eager for a closer look and squealing with pure, {{4}} joy and wonder. I found myself wondering whether the message to the next generation was less "look what robots can do" than "look what you could one day make." And after several conversations with parents, it became clear that for many Chinese families, the Robot Games could be something of a career fair for the next generation – a {{5}} of the world their children might one day help build. This year's edition, the second since the competition launched in 2025, opened Saturday evening at Beijing's National Speed Skating Oval and ran for five {{6}} days. Organized around the theme "Intelligence Competing Toward the Future," the Robot Games brought together 666 teams from 16 countries across six continents competing in 51 events with a combined total of more than 2,000 robots.
paragraphs.cn: 在北京举行的2026年世界人形机器人比赛中，机器人本应是明星，在赛道上冲刺、打破纪录、跌跌撞撞地穿越障碍赛道、进球、跳啦啦队舞，偶尔还会摇摇晃晃地完成比赛。但在拥挤的看台和不断的演示中，另一个景象吸引了我的目光——观众中大量的孩子兴奋地挤在围栏边，渴望看得更近，发出纯粹、毫无掩饰的喜悦和惊奇尖叫。我不禁想，传递给下一代的信息与其说是“看机器人能做什么”，不如说是“看你有一天能制造什么”。在与几位家长交谈后，我清楚地意识到，对许多中国家庭来说，机器人比赛可能成为下一代的一种职业博览会——让他们一窥孩子未来可能帮助构建的世界。本届比赛是该赛事自2025年创办以来的第二届，于周六晚上在北京国家速滑馆开幕，持续了连续五天。本届比赛围绕“智能竞技，迈向未来”的主题，汇聚了来自六大洲16个国家的666支队伍，参加51个项目的比赛，机器人总数超过2000台。

paragraphs.en: Ahead of the Games, organizers noted that two- and three-person ticket {{7}} were among the most popular options, with sales patterns pointing to families, friends and colleagues attending in groups. Officials {{8}} the multi-person tickets explicitly as a way to make watching the competition a family activity, describing the event as offering both a science lesson and a shared outing. That {{9}} seemed to hold up once the Games opened. Interestingly, the crowd was indeed increasingly made up of elementary-school-aged children, drawn not only to the competitions themselves but to the {{10}} exhibits on site – robots breakdancing, cooking, making coffee and drinks – and fueling a steady stream of purchases of robot-themed toys and merchandise. I saw the same pattern up close.
paragraphs.cn: 在比赛开始前，组织者指出，两人和三人套票是最受欢迎的选择之一，销售模式表明家庭、朋友和同事会组团参加。官员们明确将多人票作为一种让观看比赛成为家庭活动的方式，称该活动既提供科学课，又提供共享出游。这一框架在比赛开幕后似乎得到了证实。有趣的是，观众确实越来越多地由小学年龄段的孩子组成，他们不仅被比赛本身吸引，还被现场的互动展品吸引——机器人跳霹雳舞、烹饪、制作咖啡和饮料——并推动了机器人主题玩具和商品的热销。我近距离看到了同样的模式。

paragraphs.en:
For one parent, the trip was about giving her 7-year-old son a {{11}} sense of where technology is heading:
"I wanted him to see what technology is actually becoming, rather than only learning about it from his books or the internet. He's been very curious from such a young age, so we think maybe one day he'll be the person building these robots."
A humanoid robot is lifted above the arena during the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games, with spectators watching in the background, August 25, 2026. Qu Bo
That {{12}} echoed across. Robotics, AI and STEM aren't {{13}} national priorities to these parents. They're dinner-table conversation, extracurricular budgeting, and now, weekend outings.
paragraphs.cn: 对于一位家长来说，这次出行是为了让她7岁的儿子对技术的走向有具体的感知：“我想让他看到技术实际上正在变成什么，而不是仅仅从书本或互联网上了解。他这么小就很好奇，所以我们想也许有一天他会成为制造这些机器人的人。”一个人形机器人被举过竞技场，背景是观看的观众，2026年8月25日，曲波摄。这种情绪在各地回荡。对这些家长来说，机器人、人工智能和STEM并不是抽象的国家优先事项。它们是餐桌上的话题、课外预算，现在是周末出游。

paragraphs.en:
Another parent framed it in more competitive terms, worried about her kids falling behind peers already {{14}} in the field:
"There are so many children learning programming and robotics now. If she is interested, I want to give her the chance to see what other kids are doing and become a part of it from a young age."
The kids, for their part, aren't always thinking in terms of five-year plans. One boy, immersed in how the robot was trying to climb a particularly large box during the obstacle course, shared:
"I liked when they score goals and walk into the net. So funny!"
Not every parent frames the visit as {{15}}. For some, it's a fun, {{16}} outing that happens to double as inspiration.
paragraphs.cn: 另一位家长则用更具竞争性的语言表达，担心她的孩子落后于已经沉浸在该领域的同龄人：“现在有很多孩子在学习编程和机器人技术。如果她感兴趣，我想给她机会看看其他孩子在做什么，并从小成为其中一部分。”孩子们自己并不总是考虑五年计划。一个男孩沉浸在机器人试图在障碍赛中爬上一个特别大的箱子的过程中，分享道：“我喜欢他们进球和走进网里的样子。太有趣了！”并非每位家长都将这次参观视为战略性的。对一些人来说，这是一次有趣、新颖的出游，恰好也能激发灵感。

paragraphs.en:
As we amusedly watched kids swarm a cute little bot in shiny costume, another parent shared:
"My daughter thinks robots are cute, so when we saw the games were happening here, we thought, why not? It's something different from our usual weekend activities, and look how happy she is to see them up close," he said. Whether the motivation is {{17}} or casual, the pattern holds: across all days, families were a visible, {{18}} part of the audience at the Robot Games. In a country investing heavily in robotics and AI as strategic industries, it's hard not to read the presence of so many young spectators as part of a much longer {{19}} – a generation being introduced, one {{20}} weekend at a time, not just to the machines they may someday help build, but to the idea that these machines will belong in their world. Editor's note: Zaruhi Poghosyan is a multimedia editor for CGTN Digital.
paragraphs.cn: 当我们有趣地看着孩子们围着一个穿着闪亮服装的可爱小机器人时，另一位家长分享道：“我女儿觉得机器人很可爱，所以当我们看到比赛在这里举行时，我们想，为什么不呢？这和我们平时的周末活动不同，看她近距离看到它们多开心，”他说。无论动机是精心计算还是随意，模式都一样：在所有的日子里，家庭都是机器人比赛中可见的、有意的观众群体。在一个将机器人和人工智能作为战略产业大力投资的国家，很难不将这么多年轻观众的存在视为一个更长管道的一部分——一代人，通过一个个睁大眼睛的周末，不仅被介绍给他们未来可能帮助制造的机器，还被介绍给这些机器将属于他们世界的想法。编者注：Zaruhi Poghosyan是CGTN数字频道的多媒体编辑。

paragraphs.cn: 本文属于“中国，软焦点”系列——一个慢新闻系列，通过从容的节奏和亲密的叙事，提供对中国有质感、以人为本的一瞥。

articles.fullText:
At the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, the robots were supposed to be the stars, sprinting down tracks and breaking records, stumbling through obstacle courses, scoring goals, breaking into cheerleading dances and occasionally wobbling their way through the competition.
But amid the packed stands and nonstop demonstrations, another spectacle kept catching my eye – the sheer number of children in the audience excitedly crowding the barriers, eager for a closer look and squealing with pure, unbridled joy and wonder.
I found myself wondering whether the message to the next generation was less "look what robots can do" than "look what you could one day make." And after several conversations with parents, it became clear that for many Chinese families, the Robot Games could be something of a career fair for the next generation – a glimpse of the world their children might one day help build.
This year's edition, the second since the competition launched in 2025, opened Saturday evening at Beijing's National Speed Skating Oval and ran for five consecutive days. Organized around the theme "Intelligence Competing Toward the Future," the Robot Games brought together 666 teams from 16 countries across six continents competing in 51 events with a combined total of more than 2,000 robots.
Ahead of the Games, organizers noted that two- and three-person ticket bundles were among the most popular options, with sales patterns pointing to families, friends and colleagues attending in groups. Officials pitched the multi-person tickets explicitly as a way to make watching the competition a family activity, describing the event as offering both a science lesson and a shared outing.
That framing seemed to hold up once the Games opened. Interestingly, the crowd was indeed increasingly made up of elementary-school-aged children, drawn not only to the competitions themselves but to the interactive exhibits on site – robots breakdancing, cooking, making coffee and drinks – and fueling a steady stream of purchases of robot-themed toys and merchandise.
I saw the same pattern up close. For one parent, the trip was about giving her 7-year-old son a tangible sense of where technology is heading:
"I wanted him to see what technology is actually becoming, rather than only learning about it from his books or the internet. He's been very curious from such a young age, so we think maybe one day he'll be the person building these robots."
A humanoid robot is lifted above the arena during the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games, with spectators watching in the background, August 25, 2026. Qu Bo
That sentiment echoed across. Robotics, AI and STEM aren't abstract national priorities to these parents. They're dinner-table conversation, extracurricular budgeting, and now, weekend outings. Another parent framed it in more competitive terms, worried about her kids falling behind peers already immersed in the field:
"There are so many children learning programming and robotics now. If she is interested, I want to give her the chance to see what other kids are doing and become a part of it from a young age."
The kids, for their part, aren't always thinking in terms of five-year plans. One boy, immersed in how the robot was trying to climb a particularly large box during the obstacle course, shared:
"I liked when they score goals and walk into the net. So funny!"
Not every parent frames the visit as strategic. For some, it's a fun, novel outing that happens to double as inspiration. As we amusedly watched kids swarm a cute little bot in shiny costume, another parent shared:
"My daughter thinks robots are cute, so when we saw the games were happening here, we thought, why not? It's something different from our usual weekend activities, and look how happy she is to see them up close," he said.
Whether the motivation is calculated or casual, the pattern holds: across all days, families were a visible, deliberate part of the audience at the Robot Games. In a country investing heavily in robotics and AI as strategic industries, it's hard not to read the presence of so many young spectators as part of a much longer pipeline – a generation being introduced, one wide-eyed weekend at a time, not just to the machines they may someday help build, but to the idea that these machines will belong in their world.
Editor's note: Zaruhi Poghosyan is a multimedia editor for CGTN Digital. This article is part of China, Soft Focus – a slow journalism series that offers textured, human-centered glimpses into China through measured pace and intimate storytelling.

在比赛开始前，组织者指出，两人和三人套票是最受欢迎的选择之一，销售模式表明家庭、朋友和同事会组团参加。官员们明确将多人票作为一种让观看比赛成为家庭活动的方式，称该活动既提供科学课，又提供共享出游。这一框架在比赛开幕后似乎得到了证实。有趣的是，观众确实越来越多地由小学年龄段的孩子组成，他们不仅被比赛本身吸引，还被现场的互动展品吸引——机器人跳霹雳舞、烹饪、制作咖啡和饮料——并推动了机器人主题玩具和商品的热销。我近距离看到了同样的模式。

对于一位家长来说，这次出行是为了让她7岁的儿子对技术的走向有具体的感知：“我想让他看到技术实际上正在变成什么，而不是仅仅从书本或互联网上了解。他这么小就很好奇，所以我们想也许有一天他会成为制造这些机器人的人。”一个人形机器人被举过竞技场，背景是观看的观众，2026年8月25日，曲波摄。这种情绪在各地回荡。对这些家长来说，机器人、人工智能和STEM并不是抽象的国家优先事项。它们是餐桌上的话题、课外预算，现在是周末出游。

另一位家长则用更具竞争性的语言表达，担心她的孩子落后于已经沉浸在该领域的同龄人：“现在有很多孩子在学习编程和机器人技术。如果她感兴趣，我想给她机会看看其他孩子在做什么，并从小成为其中一部分。”孩子们自己并不总是考虑五年计划。一个男孩沉浸在机器人试图在障碍赛中爬上一个特别大的箱子的过程中，分享道：“我喜欢他们进球和走进网里的样子。太有趣了！”并非每位家长都将这次参观视为战略性的。对一些人来说，这是一次有趣、新颖的出游，恰好也能激发灵感。

当我们有趣地看着孩子们围着一个穿着闪亮服装的可爱小机器人时，另一位家长分享道：“我女儿觉得机器人很可爱，所以当我们看到比赛在这里举行时，我们想，为什么不呢？这和我们平时的周末活动不同，看她近距离看到它们多开心，”他说。无论动机是精心计算还是随意，模式都一样：在所有的日子里，家庭都是机器人比赛中可见的、有意的观众群体。在一个将机器人和人工智能作为战略产业大力投资的国家，很难不将这么多年轻观众的存在视为一个更长管道的一部分——一代人，通过一个个睁大眼睛的周末，不仅被介绍给他们未来可能帮助制造的机器，还被介绍给这些机器将属于他们世界的想法。编者注：Zaruhi Poghosyan是CGTN数字频道的多媒体编辑。

本文属于“中国，软焦点”系列——一个慢新闻系列，通过从容的节奏和亲密的叙事，提供对中国有质感、以人为本的一瞥。

articles.title: Foreign experts explain hurdles in China-Nepal border mudslide rescue
articles.titleCn: 外国专家解析中尼边境泥石流救援中的障碍

paragraphs.en: Over a week after a {{0}} mudslide, {{1}} by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on August 26, search and rescue operations there have kicked into higher gear. paragraphs.cn: 8月26日，中国西南部西藏自治区中尼边境的吉隆口岸遭遇由高海拔冰川崩塌引发的灾难性泥石流，一周多后，那里的搜救行动已进入更高强度阶段。中国救援队克服了道路损毁、地形崎岖等挑战后，于周三上午全面重新开放通往吉隆口岸的唯一陆路通道，使救援人员、救援物资、设备和重型机械能够通过公路抵达核心灾区，开展更密集的救援行动。救援人员仍面临灾区恶劣条件，各队伍部署地面雷达和空中勘测来监测边坡变形及其他潜在次生灾害，并确保搜救行动的安全。2026年9月2日，救援人员在中国西南部西藏自治区吉隆口岸灾区进行搜救行动。面对如此复杂多变的灾害条件，国际灾害管理专家强调了正在进行的边境救援行动前所未有的困难，同时肯定了中国强大的应急响应能力。

paragraphs.en: Akhilesh Surjan, a specialist in {{11}} and disaster emergency management at Australia's Charles Darwin University, stressed the necessity of sustained, {{9}} search efforts amid lingering uncertainties. In highly complex cascading catastrophes like this cross-border glacial mudslide, life-search operations must continue as long as {{10}} survival possibilities remain, Surjan said, adding that the absence of survivors in one spot cannot rule out survival chances in other buried areas. "Every search decision carries profound humanitarian and {{12}} implications for cross-border disaster relief," Surjan told The Straits Times. Winston Chang, former global lead of the UN International Search and Rescue Advisory Group, pointed out that the unique {{13}} aftermath of glacial mudslides creates enormous operational hurdles, even for well-equipped rescue forces such as China's. Powerful glacial mudslides can sweep buildings and debris several kilometers downstream, completely altering the original terrain.
paragraphs.cn: 澳大利亚查尔斯达尔文大学人道主义和灾害应急管理专家Akhilesh Surjan强调，在持续的不确定性中，必须进行持续、细致的搜索工作。Surjan表示，在像这次跨境冰川泥石流这样高度复杂的级联灾害中，只要存在可信的生存可能性，生命搜索行动就必须继续，并补充说，一个地点没有幸存者并不能排除其他掩埋区域的生存机会。Surjan告诉《海峡时报》：“每一次搜索决策都对跨境灾害救援产生深远的人道主义和外ed交影响。”联合国国际搜救咨询小组前全球负责人Winston Chang指出，冰川泥石流独特的地质后果为即使像中国这样装备精良的救援力量也带来了巨大的行动障碍。强大的冰川泥石流可以将建筑物和碎片冲到下游数公里处，完全改变原有地形。

paragraphs.en: Rescuers face great uncertainty over what lies beneath layers of deep, fluid mud and mixed rock fragments, Chang explained. He added that the unstable terrain creates a "{{14}} nightmare" for on-site operations. Specialized safety equipment, including fixed anchor points and safety ropes, is mandatory for every forward movement, he said, stressing that safety management stands as the top priority throughout the entire rescue process. People commute across the Trishuli River via an installed zip line in the aftermath of flash floods at Trishuli Center in Nepal's Nuwakot district, September 4, 2026. Echoing the view, Surjan noted that the ongoing rainfall, poor visibility, fragile mountain slopes and frequent secondary geological hazards constitute compound risks that threaten rescue personnel and slow down operational progress.
paragraphs.cn: Chang解释说，救援人员对深层流动泥浆和混合岩石碎片下的事物面临巨大不确定性。他补充说，不稳定的地形为现场行动创造了“后勤噩梦”。他说，每次前进都必须配备专业安全设备，包括固定锚点和安全绳，并强调在整个救援过程中，安全管理是首要任务。2026年9月4日，在尼泊尔努瓦科特区特里苏利中心的暴洪过后，人们通过安装的滑索穿越特里苏利河。Surjan赞同这一观点，指出持续的降雨、低能见度、脆弱的山坡和频繁的次生地质灾害构成了复合风险，威胁救援人员并减缓行动进展。

paragraphs.en: Beyond on-site rescue difficulties, the rare, sudden nature of high-altitude glacial disasters also exposes systemic gaps in global early warning systems, according to newly published research. An article published in Nature on Wednesday highlighted the urgent need to upgrade future monitoring and forecasting systems. The disaster proved difficult to predict because it was triggered by the sudden failure of a high-altitude glacier-rock system rather than typical signals, such as extreme rainfall or rising glacial lakes, according to the article. Manoochehr Shirzaei, a geophysicist at Virginia Tech, emphasized the limitations of traditional ground-monitoring technologies in tackling emerging climate-driven geological risks. Conventional monitoring systems fail to detect early signs of high-altitude glacial-rock slope instability.
paragraphs.cn: 根据新发表的研究，除了现场救援困难外，高海拔冰川灾害的罕见性和突发性也暴露了全球预警系统的系统性缺陷。周三发表在《自然》杂志上的一篇文章强调，迫切需要升级未来的监测和预测系统。文章称，这场灾害难以预测，因为它是由高海拔冰川岩石系统的突然失效引发的，而不是典型的信号，如极端降雨或冰川湖上升。弗吉尼亚理工大学地球物理学家Manoochehr Shirzaei强调了传统地面监测技术在应对新兴气候驱动地质风险方面的局限性。传统监测系统无法检测高海拔冰川岩石边坡不稳定的早期迹象。

paragraphs.en: There is an urgent demand for integrated, space-based observation networks to fill the gap, Shirzaei told Nature. The Nature study further proposed a systematic solution, "What is still largely missing is a regional satellite-based system that routinely searches for accelerating glacier and rock-slope deformation and then connects that information directly to downstream flood and avalanche modeling."
paragraphs.cn: Shirzaei告诉《自然》杂志，迫切需要综合的、基于空间的观测网络来填补这一空白。《自然》研究进一步提出了一个系统性解决方案：“目前仍然很大程度上缺失的是一个区域性的卫星系统，该系统定期搜索加速的冰川和岩石边坡变形，然后将该信息直接连接到下游洪水和雪崩建模。”

articles.fullText:
Over a week after a catastrophic mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on August 26, search and rescue operations there have kicked into higher gear.
Chinese rescue teams fully reopened the only land route to Gyirong Port on Wednesday morning after overcoming challenges such as damaged roads, rugged terrain and other obstacles, allowing rescuers, relief supplies, equipment and heavy machinery to reach the core disaster area by road to carry out more intensive rescue operations.
Rescuers still face difficult conditions in the disaster area, with teams deploying ground radar and aerial surveys to monitor slope deformation and other potential secondary disasters and help ensure the safety of search and rescue operations.
Rescue personnel conduct search and rescue operations in the disaster-hit area of Gyirong Port, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, September 2, 2026. 
Against such complex and volatile disaster conditions, international disaster management experts have highlighted the unprecedented difficulties of the ongoing border rescue operations while acknowledging China's robust emergency response capacity.
Akhilesh Surjan, a specialist in humanitarian and disaster emergency management at Australia's Charles Darwin University, stressed the necessity of sustained, meticulous search efforts amid lingering uncertainties.
In highly complex cascading catastrophes like this cross-border glacial mudslide, life-search operations must continue as long as credible survival possibilities remain, Surjan said, adding that the absence of survivors in one spot cannot rule out survival chances in other buried areas.
"Every search decision carries profound humanitarian and diplomatic implications for cross-border disaster relief," Surjan told The Straits Times.
Winston Chang, former global lead of the UN International Search and Rescue Advisory Group, pointed out that the unique geological aftermath of glacial mudslides creates enormous operational hurdles, even for well-equipped rescue forces such as China's.
Powerful glacial mudslides can sweep buildings and debris several kilometers downstream, completely altering the original terrain. Rescuers face great uncertainty over what lies beneath layers of deep, fluid mud and mixed rock fragments, Chang explained.
He added that the unstable terrain creates a "logistical nightmare" for on-site operations.
Specialized safety equipment, including fixed anchor points and safety ropes, is mandatory for every forward movement, he said, stressing that safety management stands as the top priority throughout the entire rescue process.
People commute across the Trishuli River via an installed zip line in the aftermath of flash floods at Trishuli Center in Nepal's Nuwakot district, September 4, 2026. 
Echoing the view, Surjan noted that the ongoing rainfall, poor visibility, fragile mountain slopes and frequent secondary geological hazards constitute compound risks that threaten rescue personnel and slow down operational progress.
Beyond on-site rescue difficulties, the rare, sudden nature of high-altitude glacial disasters also exposes systemic gaps in global early warning systems, according to newly published research.
An article published in Nature on Wednesday highlighted the urgent need to upgrade future monitoring and forecasting systems.
The disaster proved difficult to predict because it was triggered by the sudden failure of a high-altitude glacier-rock system rather than typical signals, such as extreme rainfall or rising glacial lakes, according to the article.
Manoochehr Shirzaei, a geophysicist at Virginia Tech, emphasized the limitations of traditional ground-monitoring technologies in tackling emerging climate-driven geological risks.
Conventional monitoring systems fail to detect early signs of high-altitude glacial-rock slope instability. There is an urgent demand for integrated, space-based observation networks to fill the gap, Shirzaei told Nature.
The Nature study further proposed a systematic solution, "What is still largely missing is a regional satellite-based system that routinely searches for accelerating glacier and rock-slope deformation and then connects that information directly to downstream flood and avalanche modeling."

articles.title: China steps up monitoring of risk areas in mudslide-hit Gyirong
articles.titleCn: 中国加强对泥石流受灾地区吉隆的风险监测
articles.summary: More than 2,300 rescuers, including 726 personnel from the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the People's Armed Police Force have joined search and rescue operations at mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region.
articles.summaryCn: 中国在西藏吉隆口岸泥石流灾害后加强救援与监测，部署无人机和雷达系统，并确保堰塞湖及冰川湖稳定。

paragraphs.en: More than 2,300 {{1}}, including 726 personnel from the Chinese People's Liberation Army and the People's Armed Police Force, have joined search and rescue {{2}} at mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. The mudslide, {{3}} by a high-altitude glacier {{4}} in Nepal on August 26, has left 31 people dead and 531 others missing in Xizang as of Saturday, according to the local emergency response and rescue command center. So far, more than 400 vehicles, more than 8,000 sets of rescue equipment and over 800 drones have been {{5}} for deeper search operations. In addition, charitable donations for relief efforts following the massive mudslide have {{6}} 660 million yuan (about $98.34 million), according to China's Ministry of Civil Affairs. Authorities have {{7}} and monitored 112 potential hazard sites, {{8}} a total of 58 geological hazard sites, including 7 high-risk areas.
paragraphs.cn: 超过2300名救援人员，包括中国人民解放军和人民武装警察部队的726名人员，已加入西藏自治区西南部吉隆口岸泥石流灾害的搜救行动。据当地应急响应和救援指挥中心称，8月26日尼泊尔高海拔冰川崩塌引发的泥石流，截至周六已造成西藏31人死亡，531人失踪。目前，已部署超过400辆车辆、8000多套救援设备和800多架无人机进行更深层次的搜索行动。此外，据中国民政部称，大规模泥石流后用于救援工作的慈善捐款已超过6.6亿元人民币（约9834万美元）。当局已检查并监测了112个潜在危险地点，共识别出58个地质灾害点，其中包括7个高风险区域。

paragraphs.en:

Delegates attend the SCO Media and Think Tank Summit at the Ala-Archa State Residence in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, July 27, 2026. 
As Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) leaders prepare to gather in Bishkek, capital of Kyrgyzstan, for summit events starting August 31, the group's 25th anniversary is drawing attention to a fast-growing area of cooperation: the digital economy.
Two new platforms launched this year show how that cooperation is moving from policy discussions toward practical projects.
At the 2026 World Intelligent Industry Expo in Tianjin in May, the SCO Digital Intelligence Application Joint Laboratory and the SCO Computing Power Industry Alliance were unveiled. Six projects worth more than 100 million yuan ($14 million) in total were also signed, according to The People's Daily Overseas Edition.
The two platforms address different needs. The laboratory focuses on turning digital technologies into real-world applications, while the alliance aims to improve access to computing power – the processing capacity needed to run AI, cloud services and other data-heavy technologies.
Zhu Shuai, a researcher at the China Center for Information Industry Development, said the two platforms feature two core elements of digital transformation: computing power and practical applications. Their launch, he said, marks a shift in SCO digital cooperation from building consensus to putting projects into practice.
Physical connections are already part of that shift. China has participated in fiber-optic projects linking China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan that have cut regional network latency by 40%, according to The People's Daily. Faster connections make it easier to move the large volumes of data required by cloud computing and AI services.
The computing alliance could take that a step further by helping participating countries share computing resources across borders. In the longer term, such coordination could help narrow gaps in access to advanced computing capacity across the region.
But connecting hardware is only part of the challenge. Countries also need compatible technical rules and useful applications.
That was a focus of the China-SCO Digital Technology Cooperation and Development Forum held in June in Karamay, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. Sessions covered communications and computing infrastructure, AI applications and the mutual recognition of standards.
China's National Data Administration said this month that cooperation with SCO countries is expanding through projects in digital infrastructure, technology applications, data connectivity and industrial digitalization. The new joint laboratory in Tianjin is among the platforms supporting that work.
The next test is whether these separate pieces can work together across countries with different levels of digital development and different technical standards.
For the SCO, that means the next phase is not simply about building more projects. It is about connecting networks, computing capacity and standards so that data and digital services can move more easily across borders.
If that happens, the roads and trade routes connecting the region could increasingly be joined by another layer of infrastructure – one built to carry data and support AI-driven services.
